question: For optimal absorption, levothyroxine should be taken:

answers.text: With milk or a calcium-containing meal to improve bioavailability

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Calcium (in milk, antacids, or supplements) chelates levothyroxine and reduces its absorption significantly — always separate by at least 4 hours.

answers.text: 30–60 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! An empty stomach in the morning (or bedtime, >3 h after dinner) maximises absorption. Co-administration with food, calcium, iron, or antacids reduces bioavailability.

answers.text: Immediately after dinner with the evening meal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Levothyroxine is best taken on an empty stomach. Bedtime dosing is acceptable only if taken >3 h after the last meal.

answers.text: Simultaneously with ferrous sulphate to improve compliance

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Iron (ferrous sulphate) forms an insoluble complex with levothyroxine, reducing absorption. They must be separated by at least 4 hours.

overallFeedback.feedback: Levothyroxine has narrow therapeutic index. Always take 30–60 min before breakfast (or bedtime) and separate from calcium, iron, and antacids by ≥4 hours.
Correct! Consistent fasting administration is critical for predictable TSH control.
